quote_original: Then I seemed to be walking in the night.
context_before: e exaltation of those who had been conquerors in a conflict with death, were singing “He is risen – He is risen” and intuitively I knew they meant me.
context_after: I soon came upon a scene that might have been the ancient Pool of Bethesda, for in this place lay a great multitude of impotent folk – blind, halt, withered – waiting not for the moving of the water as of tradition, but waiting for me. As I came near, without thought or effort on my part they were, one after the other, molded as by the Magician of the Beautiful. Eyes, hands, feet – all missing members – were drawn from some invisible reservoir and molded in harmony with that perfection which I felt springing within me. When all were made perfect, the chorus exulted, “It is finished”
selection_note: Mystical account of union with the Greater Self, vision of the Pool of Bethesda, and transformation through concept of self.

quote_original: It is a mirror to all.
context_before: As a man I conceived of It as love and myself the son of It, and in my union with It, now, what a love enfolds me!
context_after: Whatever we conceive It as being, that It is to us.

quote_original: Then there appeared before my eyes a rock of quartz crystal.
context_before: I seemed to be surrounded by luminous clouds which emanated from my head as fiery, pulsating rings. I saw nothing but these luminous rings for a time.
context_after: While I gazed upon it, the crystal broke into pieces which invisible hands quickly shaped into the living Buddha. As I looked on this meditative figure, I saw that it was myself. I was the living Buddha whom I contemplated. A light like the sun glowed from this living image of myself with increasing intensity until it exploded. Then the light gradually faded and once more I was back within the blackness of my room.
selection_note: Mystical account of union with the Greater Self, vision of the Pool of Bethesda, and transformation through concept of self.

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: So exalted were my feelings, I felt related to the stars.
context_before: The first time I awoke the fires within me I thought my head would explode. There was intense vibration at the base of my skull, then sudden oblivion of all. Then I found myself clothed in a garment of light and attached by a silvery elastic cord to the slumbering body on the bed.
context_after: In this garment I roamed spheres more familiar than earth, but found that, as on earth, conditions were molded in harmony with my nature.
selection_note: Mystical account of union with the Greater Self, vision of the Pool of Bethesda, and transformation through concept of self.

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: What we imagine, that we are.
context_before: I am an immortal being conceiving myself as man and forming worlds in the likeness and image of my concept of self.
context_after: By our imagination, we have created this dream of life, and by our imagination we will re-enter that eternal world of light, becoming that which we were before we imagined the world.
selection_note: Mystical account of union with the Greater Self, vision of the Pool of Bethesda, and transformation through concept of self.

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: First published 1946 in the United States; copyright not renewed under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: They reveal our concepts of ourselves.
context_before: The pictures and circumstances we see in dreams are creations of our own imagination and have no existence save in ourselves. The same is true of the pictures and circumstances we see in this dream of life.
context_after: As soon as we succeed in transforming self, our world will dissolve and reshape itself in harmony with that which our change affirms.
selection_note: Mystical account of union with the Greater Self, vision of the Pool of Bethesda, and transformation through concept of self.
